name: Ambelau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Collins 1981/1983 classification refs on Glottolog; Grimes SIL fieldwork unpublished; no grammar/phonology naming stress found

sources.citation: Stokhof, W. A. L. (ed.). 1982. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia, vol. 3/4: Central Moluccas: Ambon (II), Buru, Nusa Laut, Saparua (Pacific Linguistics D-50). Canberra: ANU. Ambelau list 55d (NBG 1896), pp. 49-58.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bare 1896 wordlist in Dutch-based spelling; no stress marks, no notes on accent.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification (Languages of the New Guinea Region 1). Berlin: Language Science Press. §9.2 Ambelau, pp. 374-378.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ambelau section (pp. 374-378) is historical phonology and subgrouping only (*p > f, *t > tʃ/r, *w > β, etc.); no statement of Ambelau stress placement. The only stress remarks are general (Aru transcription convention, p. 87/§6: 'the normal pattern is penultimate stress'), not about Ambelau.

sources.citation: Sumarlam, Dwi Purnanto, Burhanuddin & Hujaefa H. Muhammad. 2018. Reflex Proto-Austronesia to Ambelau in West Central Maluku group: the effort to test the hypothesis Collins (1981). Proceedings of PRASASTI 2018 (ASSEHR 166), 307-315. DOI 10.2991/prasasti-18.2018.58.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Gives Ambelau phoneme inventory citing Sumarlam et al. 2017 (19 consonants, 8 vowels /i u e ə ɛ o ɔ a/, 2 diphthongs) and PAN reflexes by position (initial/penultimate/ultimate syllable); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Sumarlam, Djatmika, Dwi Purnanto & Burhanuddin. 2017. Urgensi studi linguistik historis terhadap kelompok Maluku Tengah Barat: beberapa catatan studi pendahuluan Collins (1981). Arkhais: Jurnal Ilmu Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia 8(2): 101-110.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Review of Collins's subgrouping evidence; no phonological description of Ambelau beyond reflexes, nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/aksen/stress empty).

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 2000. Defining speech communities on Buru Island: a look at both linguistic and non-linguistic factors. In C. E. Grimes (ed.), Spices from the east (Pacific Linguistics 503), 73-103. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; §7.4.1 Ambelau (p. 100) gives villages, 5,700 speakers, non-intelligibility with Buru; Ambelau wordlist by Edgar Travis (Oct 1986); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Taber, Mark (ed.). 1996. Atlas bahasa tanah Maluku. Ambon: PPPM Universitas Pattimura & SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog overview reference; an atlas, so unlikely to state stress, but not checked because the SIL PDF could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1983. The historical relationships of the languages of Central Maluku, Indonesia (Pacific Linguistics D-47). Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Ambelau stress rule. p. 67 (on Stresemann's stress-conditioned split of *a in Buru dialects): 'He suggests a similar conditioning rule for Ambelau but offers little evidence' and reports Ambelau (Wailua) *a > e without a stress split. Penultimate-stress statements in the book concern Hoamoal/Asilulu (p. 130ff), not Ambelau.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1982. Prothesis in the languages of Central Maluku: an argument from Proto-Austronesian grammar. Pacific Linguistics C-75 (TICAL 2), 187-200.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ambelau appears only in a bibliographic citation; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1981. Preliminary notes on Proto-West Central Maluku: Buru, Sula, Taliabo and Ambelau. In R. A. Blust (ed.), Historical linguistics in Indonesia, Part I (NUSA 10), 31-45. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Scan with no text layer; scanned. Sound correspondences and subgrouping evidence only; no mention of stress/accent for Ambelau.

sources.citation: Labbineka / Peta Bahasa (Badan Bahasa), 'Bahasa Ambalau' entry (id 338).
sources.note: Location (Desa Ulima, Kec. Ambalau, Buru Selatan) and dialectometry only; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en, ru, id) articles 'Ambelau language' / 'Bahasa Ambalau'.
sources.note: No phonology section in any of the three; cite Ethnologue, Grimes & Edwards, SIL only.

sources.citation: Balai Bahasa Provinsi Maluku. Kamus Ambalau-Indonesia and Kamus Percakapan Ambalau-Indonesia (in preparation; data collection Feb 2026, target publication end 2026).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Badan Bahasa bilingual dictionaries normally open with a fonologi/ejaan section that states tekanan kata; would be the first modern first-hand description.

sources.citation: Erniati. 2020. Kekerabatan bahasa Ambalau dan bahasa Buru berdasarkan daftar 200 kosakata dasar Swadesh: kajian leksikostatistik. Gramatika 8(1): 60-73.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only recent Indonesian first-hand data on Ambalau (Kantor Bahasa Maluku fieldwork, Desa Ulima); lexicostatistic, so a stress statement is unlikely but the wordlist may be transcribed with stress.

sources.citation: Sumarlam, Dwi Purnanto, Burhanuddin et al. 2017. Menguji hipotesis Collins (1981) tentang keberadaan Kelompok Maluku Tengah Barat. Laporan Penelitian Hibah Pascasarjana 2017 Menristekdikti, Universitas Sebelas Maret, Surakarta.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cited in Sumarlam et al. 2018 as the source of the synchronic Ambelau phoneme inventory (19 C, 8 V, 2 diphthongs) from 2017 fieldwork; a synchronic phonology of this kind may include a stress statement.

sources.citation: Travis, Edgar (Ed). 1986. Ambelau word list (6 October 1986). Unpublished SIL field data, cited in Grimes 2000 and Grimes & Edwards 2026.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Primary field transcription of Ambelau by an SIL linguist; may carry stress marking or notes; basis of the Ambelau data in Grimes & Edwards 2026.

sources.citation: Stresemann, Erwin. 1927. Die Lauterscheinungen in den ambonischen Sprachen (Beihefte zur Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen 10). Berlin: Reimer.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only work reported to discuss stress in Ambelau: Collins 1983:67 says Stresemann posits a stress-conditioned vowel split for Sub-Buru and 'suggests a similar conditioning rule for Ambelau'. Likely contains a Betonung/Akzent remark for Ambelau (Freiburg expedition data, 1910-12).
